course_title: Business Registration & Compliance for Product Makers: NAFDAC, SON and Safe Production

say: Choose your NAFDAC route, and get your pack ready.
This is the video for module one of Business Registration and Compliance for Product Makers.

A packaged food or cosmetic needs NAFDAC approval before it is sold to the public. NAFDAC runs a special scheme for micro and small enterprises, with lower fees and simpler documents. Getting the route right saves you paying for the wrong application.

say: NAFDAC's scheme page names bread, packaged water, and kitchen-scale and micro-scale foods. On the cosmetic and household side, it lists shea butter, petroleum jelly, oils, soaps and laundry detergents, among others.

panel.heading: Does the MSME scheme accept it?

say: At micro scale, meat, milk and fish are excluded, except dried meat and dried fish, because germs grow in them quickly. Complex cosmetics, pressurised sprays and hand sanitisers do not qualify. Those go through regular registration.

panel.heading: Does the MSME scheme accept it?

say: A micro scale facility has not more than five employees.

panel.heading: The micro scale rules
items: Listing certificate valid for two years

say: It needs at least one designated room that does not open directly to a toilet, a refuse dump or an open gutter. The route depends on where you make the product, not only what it is.

say: Only five products can be registered. For example, Amaka makes seven, so she ranks them by monthly sales. Her top five are 680 of her 745 monthly units, about 91 percent. She pauses the other two.

panel.rule: The vetting sample must be exactly the product you will sell.

say: Check every label field before you print the three labels. Write the common name, not just a brand, and net weight in metric units like 200 g. List all ingredients, largest first.
Add a batch number, dates, and your full address. Reserve a space for the NAFDAC number, and never print NAFDAC approved before approval.
Set best-before from your own sealed samples, checked every two weeks, and make it shorter than the last good check.

say: Allergens are a safety field. Groundnut, sesame, wheat, egg, milk and tree nut oils like almond can cause serious reactions. If any is in your product, even a little, name it clearly.

say: The supermarket needs a NAFDAC number. A man at the market offers to arrange one in seven days, for a fee. Funmi asks: will my room be inspected and my product tested? He says no. So it is not a genuine registration.
At about 1,500 naira a pack, 300,000 naira of monthly sales could be seized, plus the supermarket relationship.
So she applies on NAFDAC's portal with her own login, pays only against an official payment advice, and keeps the buyer updated. Never pay cash for the inspector.
To remember. Check both your product type and your room. Micro scale means not more than five staff and five products. Lock your formula as weights and percentages.
Fill every label field, including allergens. And any offer that skips inspection and lab testing is not a real registration.
